title: 5. Regulatory and Compliance
subtitle: Regulation · RegTech · RBI Sandbox · AML · KYC · Tax issues
subject: FinTech

sections.heading: 5.1 FinTech Regulation Framework
sections.html:
Updated for Assessment Year 2026-27 (income of FY 2025-26, assessed under the Income-tax Act, 1961).

Objectives: understand FinTech regulation, RegTech, RBI sandbox, AML, KYC and tax issues.

Regulation balances innovation with consumer protection and stability. Indian regulators: RBI (banking, payments), SEBI (securities), IRDAI (insurance), PFRDA (pensions), IFSCA (GIFT City). Key laws: Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007, IT Act 2000, Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023.

sections.heading: 5.2 RegTech and Ecosystem
sections.html:
RegTech uses technology to automate compliance: reporting, monitoring and risk management. Players: regulated firms, RegTech vendors, regulators (SupTech).

Example: Automated systems file suspicious-transaction reports without manual effort.

sections.heading: 5.3 Financial Inclusion and Adoption
sections.html: PM Jan Dhan Yojana opened over 50 crore accounts. Adoption barriers: low literacy, language, trust, and connectivity.

sections.heading: 5.4 Role of the Central Bank and RBI Regulatory Sandbox
sections.html: The RBI issues licences, supervises payment systems and protects customers. Its Regulatory Sandbox (2019) lets firms test innovations on a limited scale, with relaxed rules, in cohorts such as retail payments, cross-border payments and MSME lending.

sections.heading: 5.5 Anti Money Laundering and Know Your Client
sections.html: AML: under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act 2002, entities must monitor and report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND. Stages of laundering: placement, layering, integration. KYC: identify customers (Aadhaar, PAN, video KYC) and re-verify periodically.

sections.heading: 5.6 Tax Issues (Assessment Year 2026-27)
sections.html:
Which law applies? Income earned in FY 2025-26 is assessed in Assessment Year 2026-27 under the Income-tax Act, 1961. The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026 and replaces "previous year" and "assessment year" with a single Tax Year; the first Tax Year is 2026-27.

IssuePosition for AY 2026-27
Income from transfer of virtual digital assets (VDA)Flat 30% under Sec 115BBH plus surcharge and cess; only the cost of acquisition is deductible
Loss on VDACannot be set off against any other income
TDS on VDA transfer1% under Sec 194S (subject to thresholds); payments to non-residents under Sec 195
ReportingSchedule VDA in the ITR; crypto-asset reporting by specified entities under Sec 285BAA
Gift of VDATaxable in the recipient's hands where the value exceeds ₹50,000
GST on FinTech service fees18%
Example: Priya buys a crypto asset for ₹1,00,000 and sells it for ₹1,40,000 in FY 2025-26. Gain = ₹40,000; tax at 30% = ₹12,000, plus 4% cess = ₹12,480 (surcharge ignored). The platform deducts 1% TDS on ₹1,40,000 = ₹1,400, which she claims as credit in her ITR for AY 2026-27. A loss on another crypto trade cannot reduce this gain.
